SoftClock3.sound: A metronome of swooping tones that synchronises humans, not machines.
SoftClock3.use: Recording to a click you can groove with. Route its audio to a track and record it.

SoftClock2.what: A groove-oriented time reference, second version.
SoftClock2.sound: Swooping tones with accents, swing and peak/valley shaping.
SoftClock2.use: Recording to a click you can groove with.

controls.Peak: Level of the high point of each beat.

SoftClock.sound: A swooping-tone metronome that synchronises humans.
SoftClock.use: Recording to a click you can groove with.

BitShiftPan.what: A gain and pan done only with bit shifts.
BitShiftPan.sound: Lossless 6 dB steps. Centre is louder than the sides; the first steps to the side are large.
BitShiftPan.use: Perfectly clean level and pan changes.

BitShiftGain.what: The perfect boost or pad, in 6 dB steps only.
BitShiftGain.sound: No maths, no dither: scaling by exactly 6 dB steps.

PurestGain.what: A high-resolution, noise-shaped gain with a smoothed fader.
PurestGain.sound: Clean gain with a slow fade for safe automation.
PurestGain.use: A clean gain utility and fades.

PurestDualPan.sound: Sine pan law as in Console9, with quick de-zippering.
PurestDualPan.use: Independent left and right gain and pan.

BitDualPan.what: A dual pan that is almost BitShiftGain.
BitDualPan.sound: Bit-shift gain and pan on each side.

PurestFade.what: Like PurestGain, but for long fades.
PurestFade.sound: Fades all the way to silence without an abrupt cut.

Monitoring3.what: Monitoring with Ten Nines into Dark as the wordlength reducer.
Monitoring3.sound: Dither to 24 or 16 bit plus mix check modes such as SubsOnly, SlewOnly and PeaksOnly.
Monitoring3.use: Last in the chain on the 2-buss, to check a mix in different ways and dither the output.

controls.Monitor: Picks the monitoring mode or output depth.

Monitoring2.what: Monitoring with Dark as the wordlength reducer.
Monitoring2.sound: Dither to 24 or 16 bit plus mix check modes such as SubsOnly, SlewOnly and PeaksOnly.
Monitoring2.use: Last in the chain on the 2-buss, to check a mix in different ways and dither the output.

controls.Monitor: Picks the monitoring mode or output depth.

Monitoring.what: Your one-stop shop for final 2-buss work.
Monitoring.sound: Dither to 24 or 16 bit plus mix check modes such as SubsOnly, SlewOnly and PeaksOnly.
Monitoring.use: Last in the chain on the 2-buss, to check a mix in different ways and dither the output.

controls.Monitor: Picks the monitoring mode or output depth.

EveryTrim.what: Left/right, mid/side and master trims in one plugin.
EveryTrim.sound: Plain, clean gain trim with noise shaping.

HermeTrim.sound: Plus or minus 12 dB of each trim, nearly as clean as PurestGain.

DubPlate2.what: Mastering for electronic music in the style of a dubplate cut.
DubPlate2.use: Giving electronic music a dubplate sound.

DubPlate.what: Ruthless dubplate mastering for electronic music.
DubPlate.sound: The sound of a cut acetate dubplate.
DubPlate.use: Retro-styled mastering of electronic music. No controls.

CansAW.what: Chris's Airwindows mix room, in a plugin, for headphone mixers.
CansAW.use: Checking a mix as if in different positions in a real room.

Cans.what: A room simulator for headphone mixers.
Cans.sound: Adjustable control-room sounds from compact to huge.
Cans.use: Mixing on headphones with a room around you.

SlewOnly.what: A mix check that shows only the extreme highs.
SlewOnly.sound: Super-bright: only the difference between samples, with no latency or ringing.
SlewOnly.use: Checking the top of a mix. No controls; don't print through it.

SubsOnly.what: A mix check that shows only the extreme lows.
SubsOnly.use: Checking the bass balance of a mix. No controls.

PeaksOnly.sound: Phase-rotates the signal so only the peaks stand out. It wrecks the sound.
PeaksOnly.use: Revealing peaks in a mix. Never master through it. No controls.

Golem.what: Blends a stereo track of two mics on an amp to mono.
Golem.sound: Mixes both mics, with a sample delay on one side to align phase.
Golem.use: Metal guitar cabs recorded with two microphones.

controls.Balance: Balance between left and right mic.
controls.Offset: Delay on one side, in samples.

DCVoltage.what: A DC control voltage, in a plugin.
DCVoltage.sound: Pure DC. Dangerous to speakers if misused.
DCVoltage.use: Cancelling DC offset or controlling a DC-coupled system. Careful.

LRConvolve3.what: Gates one channel by the other.
LRConvolve3.sound: Roughly or cleanly, depending on Smooth.

LRConvolve2.sound: Multiplies each channel by the other; Soar shows its crossover distortion.

LRConvolve.what: Multiplies each channel by the other.
LRConvolve.sound: Awful and wonderful: a sine in one channel turns a voice into the Swedish Chef.
LRConvolve.use: Wild effects on stereo pairs. No controls.

EdIsDim.what: The other half of MidSide: converts mid/side back to stereo.
EdIsDim.sound: Switches between stereo and mid/side so any plugin can process mid or side.
EdIsDim.use: Put MidSide before your processing and EdIsDim after it.

controls.ediS/diM: Balances the mid and side content.

MidSide.sound: Switches between stereo and mid/side so any plugin can process mid or side.
MidSide.use: Put MidSide before your processing and EdIsDim after it.

controls.Mid/Side: Balances the mid and side content.

uLawEncode.what: The encode half of a uLaw companding pair.
uLawEncode.sound: A reversible, distorting companding as used for telephone transmission. Much more extreme than Console.
uLawEncode.use: Use the pair for effects. Encode first, process, then decode.

uLawDecode.what: The decode half of a uLaw companding pair.
uLawDecode.sound: A reversible, distorting companding as used for telephone transmission. Much more extreme than Console.
uLawDecode.use: Use the pair for effects. Encode first, process, then decode.

RightoMono.what: Copies the right channel to both, losslessly.
RightoMono.sound: Bypasses noise on the other side.
RightoMono.use: Sources where only one side holds audio. No controls.

LeftoMono.what: Copies the left channel to both, losslessly.
LeftoMono.sound: Bypasses noise on the other side.
LeftoMono.use: Sources where only one side holds audio. No controls.

Balanced.what: Runs an XLR input into a stereo input and sums to mono.
Balanced.sound: Sums a balanced signal and cancels common noise.
Balanced.use: Using a balanced source on stereo inputs.

Flipity.what: A channel phase flipper and swapper.
Flipity.sound: Flips phase of L, R or both, swaps channels, and combinations.

controls.Flipity: Picks the flip or swap mode.

MoNoam.what: Variations on mono, mid and side in different channels.
MoNoam.sound: Switches mid/side configurations, including a mono check from one speaker.

controls.Monotor: Picks the mono, mid or side mode.

VoiceTrick.what: Lets you record vocals while monitoring over speakers.
VoiceTrick.sound: Exploits microphone and ear quirks to cancel the monitored sound in the recording.
VoiceTrick.use: Singing with monitor speakers or open-ear headphones.

DeCrackle.what: Isolates clicks and vinyl crackles to remove them.
DeCrackle.sound: A lot of work for a good purpose: cleaning vinyl. It isn't magic.

ContentHideD.what: Mutes audio except for brief glimpses.
ContentHideD.sound: Mostly silence, with blips under a second every few seconds.
ContentHideD.use: A YouTube utility so protected audio isn't flagged. No controls.
